name: KamLAND-Zen
full_name: Kamioka Liquid-scintillator Antineutrino Detector - Zero Neutrino Double-Beta Decay
summary: KamLAND-Zen dissolved enriched xenon in an inner scintillator balloon inside KamLAND to search for xenon-136 neutrinoless double-beta decay. The Zen-400 and Zen-800 datasets remain distinct from the later KamLAND2-Zen upgrade proposal.
detection_principle: Scintillation light measures the combined decay energy and reconstructed position. Event timing, spatial cuts and background models isolate xenon-136 decays within the inner balloon.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The complete KamLAND-Zen search found no neutrinoless decay and improved the combined half-life limit.

collaboration.name: KamLAND-Zen Collaboration
lead_institutions: Tohoku University Research Center for Neutrino Science
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Complete combined limit
key_parameters.value: T1/2 above 3.8 x 10^26 yr at 90% confidence

results.summary: The complete KamLAND-Zen search found no neutrinoless decay and improved the combined half-life limit.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
